NOVELTY STATEMENT — Standard practice tracks debris count/size distribution from the inductive sensor. My observable is the rate of change of debris count (debris acceleration), which provides early warning of progressive damage before catastrophic failure by indicating increasing wear rates rather than just cumulative damage.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing physical relation is that wear rate acceleration follows the Archard wear law: wear volume ∝ load × sliding distance / hardness. For a failing gear, as surface damage progresses, wear rate increases exponentially. A debris acceleration value > 0.5 particles/hour² indicates accelerating wear, which can be detected 30+ days before secondary damage occurs.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — Components: 1) Existing inductive debris sensor (particles >100μm), 2) Existing 1 Hz vibration RMS sensor, 3) Standard PLC or edge computing device. Materials: None additional. Procedure: 1) Log debris count and vibration RMS at 1 Hz, 2) Compute hourly debris count averages, 3) Calculate second derivative of debris count (debris acceleration), 4) Flag when debris acceleration exceeds threshold. All computation uses standard industrial control algorithms.

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — Installability: SAME (uses existing sensors). Operability: SAME (no additional operator training required). Maintenance: SAME (no new maintenance tasks). Cost class: SAME (no additional hardware required). The only difference is the software algorithm for debris acceleration calculation, which is negligible in cost compared to standard monitoring systems.

EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: 1) Install system on 10 turbines with known gear wear history, 2) Monitor for 12 months, 3) Record all debris acceleration events and actual failures. Instruments: Existing debris sensor and vibration sensor. Pass threshold: ≥90% of actual failures predicted ≥30 days in advance with ≤1 false alarm per turbine per year. Kill criterion: If <70% of failures are predicted with >30 days lead time OR >2 false alarms per turbine per year, the predictor is invalidated. Duration: 12 months of continuous monitoring.
